Dear Mrs. Okafor, I'm not sure you'll remember me, but I was in your 11th grade English class a long time ago. I was the kid in the back who never turned in the reading journal on time. I've been meaning to write this for years, and I'm finally doing it. You were the first teacher who ever told me my writing was worth reading. There was this essay I threw together the night before, and you wrote a note at the bottom that said something, this is the most honest thing you've written. Keep going. I kept that paper in a shoebox all through college and through two moves across country. I ended up becoming a reporter. And now I edit a little paper in the town where I live.
